statement: Let Same(p,q) be the recursive predicate: Same(Null,Null)=true; Same(Node(vp,lp,rp), Node(vq,lq,rq)) = (vp=vq and Same(lp,lq) and Same(rp,rq)); Same(p,q)=false in every other constructor case. Then is_same_tree p q returns Ok b for some Boolean b, and b=true exactly when Same(p,q) holds. Equivalently, the returned Boolean is true if and only if the two trees have identical structure and equal values at every corresponding node.
preconditions: p and q are finite binary trees satisfying the LeetCode constraints: nodes(p) <= 100, nodes(q) <= 100, and every node value of p or q lies in [-10000,10000], where nodes(Null)=0 and nodes(Node(v,l,r))=1+nodes(l)+nodes(r).

statement: For every p and q, is_same_tree p q returns Ok b for some Boolean b; it never returns Err. In particular, the call cannot fail by arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: None: p and q are arbitrary finite values of the inductive type Tree.
None (Null satisfies the LeetCode node-count and value bounds vacuously).

statement: For every v,l,r, is_same_tree Null (Node(v,l,r)) = Ok false and is_same_tree (Node(v,l,r)) Null = Ok false.
preconditions: v is any 64-bit integer and l,r are finite Tree values; under the LeetCode constraints one may additionally require -10000 <= v <= 10000 and at most 100 nodes, but the statement holds without those restrictions.

statement: For every a,b, is_same_tree (Node(a,Null,Null)) (Node(b,Null,Null)) returns Ok true exactly when a=b, and returns Ok false exactly when a!=b.
preconditions: a and b are 64-bit integers; under the LeetCode constraints they lie in [-10000,10000], but the statement holds for all 64-bit integers.

statement: For every such v1,v2,l1,r1,l2,r2, is_same_tree (Node(v1,l1,r1)) (Node(v2,l2,r2)) = Ok false.
preconditions: v1 and v2 are 64-bit integers with v1 != v2; l1,r1,l2,r2 are finite Tree values. Under LeetCode constraints the values lie in [-10000,10000], but the statement holds without that restriction.

statement: For every p,q, whenever is_same_tree p q returns Ok b, the call is_same_tree q p returns Ok b with the same Boolean b.
preconditions: p and q are finite Tree values.

statement: For every p, is_same_tree p p = Ok true.
preconditions: p is a finite Tree value.

statement: For every such v,l1,r1,l2,r2, if is_same_tree l1 l2 = Ok false, then is_same_tree (Node(v,l1,r1)) (Node(v,l2,r2)) = Ok false.
preconditions: v is a 64-bit integer; l1,r1,l2,r2 are finite Tree values.

statement: For every such v,l1,r1,l2,r2, if is_same_tree r1 r2 = Ok false, then is_same_tree (Node(v,l1,r1)) (Node(v,l2,r2)) = Ok false.
preconditions: v is a 64-bit integer; l1,r1,l2,r2 are finite Tree values.

statement: For every such v,l1,r1,l2,r2, if is_same_tree l1 l2 = Ok true and is_same_tree r1 r2 = Ok true, then is_same_tree (Node(v,l1,r1)) (Node(v,l2,r2)) = Ok true.
preconditions: v is a 64-bit integer; l1,r1,l2,r2 are finite Tree values.

statement: For every such values, if is_same_tree (Node(v1,l1,r1)) (Node(v2,l2,r2)) returns Ok true, then v1=v2, is_same_tree l1 l2 = Ok true, and is_same_tree r1 r2 = Ok true.
preconditions: v1,v2 are 64-bit integers; l1,r1,l2,r2 are finite Tree values.

statement: Define SameShape(p,q) recursively by SameShape(Null,Null)=true; SameShape(Node(u,lp,rp),Node(w,lq,rq)) = (SameShape(lp,lq) and SameShape(rp,rq)); and SameShape(p,q)=false in all other constructor cases. Whenever is_same_tree p q returns Ok true, SameShape(p,q) holds.
preconditions: p and q are finite Tree values.

statement: Define nodes(Null)=0 and nodes(Node(v,l,r))=1+nodes(l)+nodes(r). Whenever is_same_tree p q returns Ok true, nodes(p)=nodes(q).
preconditions: p and q are finite Tree values.

statement: For a finite path whose elements are L or R, define at(t,[]) to be none if t=Null and some v if t=Node(v,l,r); define at(Null,d::rest)=none; define at(Node(v,l,r),L::rest)=at(l,rest); define at(Node(v,l,r),R::rest)=at(r,rest). Whenever is_same_tree p q returns Ok false, there exists a finite path such that at(p,path) != at(q,path) as values of type Option i64.
preconditions: p and q are finite Tree values; path ranges over finite sequences of directions L and R.
